correctness.rationale: In the affine sum-one hyperplane, coordinate normals have norm sqrt(1−n^−2) and adjacent Monge normals have norm 2. Rescale any admissible ball to a nonnegative array D with all Monge slacks at least 1. The quadratic baseline D0_ij=(j−i)(j−i−1)/2 has all slacks 1 and sum T_n. Subtracting D0 yields an ordinary Monge array E, so the identity assignment is minimal and uniform averaging gives sum(E)/n >= sum(diag(E))>=0. Equality forces all diagonal entries zero and every permutation assignment tied, hence every 2x2 mixed difference vanishes and E_ij=u_i−u_j. Nonnegativity reduces to 0<=u_i−u_(i+1)<=1, giving exactly the full center cube. Exact coordinate zeros yield the facet-contact count. No finite check is substituted for this all-n proof.
